DESCRIPTION:
The check the suite's own models are deliberately unable to make.

Those models tolerate unknown fields on purpose: adding one is backwards
compatible, and a functional test has no business failing because the
application grew a column. But *somebody* has to notice, because an
undeclared field is a field no consumer was told about — and on these models
it may well be one nobody meant to publish.

will not catch this. It has to be asserted directly.

DESCRIPTION:
Asserted as an exact set, in both directions.

A removed value breaks code that produces it. An *added* value breaks code

direction violates the schema, which is precisely why the check belongs to
the consumer.
NAME: test_enum_fields_are_constrained_to_the_expected_values[CampaignOut-status]

DESCRIPTION:
The assertion that survives a rename.

A renamed field changes the response and the document together, so
conformance still passes. What does not pass is this: the consumer's own list
of what it needs, checked against what the provider now offers.

Required, not merely present: a field that became optional is a field that
can arrive missing, and every caller reading it would then break at runtime
rather than here.
NAME: test_the_fields_this_suite_reads_are_declared_and_required[DeliveryOut]

NAME: test_a_sent_campaign_cannot_be_reopened

Asserting only that a viewer sees no buttons would pass just as well against

makes the viewer's absence mean something.
NAME: test_a_viewer_sees_no_write_controls[chromium]

The rates are the numbers a person would quote, so they are the ones most

NAME: test_gt_compares_numerically_rather_than_as_text

The same 404-not-403 rule as contacts, across the other two modules.

Isolation implemented per-endpoint tends to be implemented per-endpoint

pass for security.

NAME: test_the_funnel_never_widens_as_it_deepens

DESCRIPTION:
Deep-linking past the login screen must not work.

Every route in the application is reachable by URL, which is exactly why the
guard has to live in the router rather than in the links: hiding a nav item
does nothing for someone who types the address.
NAME: test_an_unauthenticated_visitor_is_redirected_to_login[chromium]

DESCRIPTION:
The search box is reached by its label, the way a person finds it — and
the term arrives from the URL, proving the grid reads its state from there
rather than only from the control.
NAME: test_a_deep_link_applies_a_search_term[chromium]

DESCRIPTION:
A well-formed response with nothing in it.

Worth its own test because "no rows" and "broken" render almost the same

NAME: test_an_empty_result_shows_the_empty_state_not_an_error[chromium]

DESCRIPTION:
The accessible view of the same data.

Two renderings of one payload are two chances to disagree, and the table is
the one someone using a screen reader gets — so it is the one that must not
quietly drift.
NAME: test_the_table_view_matches_the_intercepted_payload[chromium]

DESCRIPTION:
401, and no token in the body.

The second assertion is the one worth having. A endpoint that returns 401

check and be a complete authentication bypass.
NAME: test_login_with_a_wrong_password_is_rejected

DESCRIPTION:

counts in the same response rather than against anything remembered.
NAME: test_rates_are_consistent_with_the_counts_they_summarise

NAME: test_an_editor_cannot_delete_a_contact
